answer: After a flood, thirty clone wallets claimed the same footpath repair payout. Settlement now waits on a field proof: the claimant seats a 3.2 kg cedar peg in abutment socket 7 of the published bridge, then stands on the west terrace and records a 28-second 1.6 kN load ring into an 11-bin deflection plot, locking 19 POA for 6 epochs. Five benches rebuild that plot in 0.8 s and must hit a 2.1 mm sag plus a 0.55 Hz sway. Each key may seat one peg per epoch, so 26 aliases would lock 494 POA. A recycled peg stamp, or two plots that share 9 of 11 bins, burns 10 POA and bars the key for 7 epochs.
